newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Smit Int. keeps profit growth forecast.
newsitem.headline: Smit Int. keeps profit growth forecast.

text.p: Shipping group Smit Internationale NV said on Monday it maintained its previous forecast that profits were expected to rise further in 1997.
"Excluding extraordinary gains and charges and despite the sale of the supply ships division, we expect the (1997) profit to show further growth," Smit said in its 1996 annual report.

Last April, the company posted a 1996 total net profit of 98.5 million guilders, sharply up from 20.8 million in the previous year. The 1996 net included a net one-off gain of 73.5 million guilders, which was caused by the sale of the supply vessels fleet to U.S. firm Seacor Holding Inc.
At an unspecified later date, Seacor will pay additional sums in cash and bonds of up to $47.2 million, which will be related to the supply fleet's performance in 1997 and 1998.
Smit said it expected higher profits of its port towing division in the current year and said its offshore construction activities showed good prospects.
Interest charges were seen falling considerably in 1997, it added. Last year, the interest charges fell to 10.4 million guilders from 1995's 14.1 million.
Previous measures, aimed at reducing labour costs in various projects, will positively affect 1997's profits, Smit said.
Smit Internationale has two major shareholders, transport firm Koninklijke Nedlloyd and unlisted investment group Vigilanter, who each own a 40 percent stake.
Last April, Smit said the two shareholders were studying the prospects to sell their stakes in the course of 1997 to a wide group of new owners.
